title: Headless judge and label drains deadlock the daemon: spawnSync blocks the event loop while the spawned child calls back over HTTP
summary: CONFIRMED root cause (symptom: daemon froze and blocked all work after a 5-min drain tick). lib/headless-drain.js runDrain uses spawnSync, which blocks the daemon's single-threaded Node event loop for the entire child run. The JUDGE drain spawns a headless claude -p that must call GET /judge/next + POST /judge/verdict back on the SAME daemon, and the LABEL drain's gate-label.js also talks HTTP to it — but a daemon frozen in spawnSync cannot serve those callbacks, so the child hangs until the 10-min timeout and writes nothing. The LEARNER drain survives only because it writes a JSON file and does not call back to the daemon, which is exactly why the learner-first design passed review while judge/label silently fail in production. The 40 unit tests MOCK spawnSync, so none exercised a real child calling into a frozen daemon (unit-green, integration-broken). Secondary finding: the headless claude -p judge is a FULL Claude Code session — captured stdout shows it running SessionStart hooks; even with a free daemon it spent 75s in startup without reaching judging, so each run is minutes. THE FIX: convert runDrain (and runDueDrains) from spawnSync to async child_process.spawn so the daemon event loop stays free to serve the drains' HTTP callbacks; update the governor accounting + the daemon.js trigger to the async shape; replace the spawnSync mocks in test/headless-drain.test.js with an integration test that exercises a real callback. CURRENT STATE: feature is merged to main (8e9024a) but DISABLED — ORCH_HEADLESS_DRAINS set to 0 in .mcp.json and .claude/settings.json, daemon relaunched flag-off (PID 51368). Do NOT re-enable the flag until the async-spawn fix lands. DEPENDENCY (build into bin/install.js): turning headless judge drains on requires the Claude Code CLI installed AND authenticated (the runner spawns claude -p, resolved via lib/claude-cli.js); the installer must verify/wire this, plus stop clobbering .mcp.json env on reinstall and add a --headless-drains opt-in.
